video_title: Derrick White On Defending Wemby, Mazzulla Learning From WWE & What We Don't Know About Jaylen Brown

quotes.speaker: Derrick White
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White on the challenge of defending Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: You've never really seen someone that size that can handle, can shoot from the perimeter.
quotes.quote: You want to be physical, but you've never really seen someone that size that can handle, can shoot from the perimeter. If you want to put a big on him, he's going to take him in the perimeter and you're going to have to guard him out there. If you want to guard him the small, then he can just throw it up to him and let him be tall. He's one of a kind.

quotes.speaker: Derrick White
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White on the best defensive approach for Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: I think I would start Chet Holmgren on him. He's one of the best defenders in the league.
quotes.quote: Personally, I think I would start Chet Holmgren on him. He's one of the best defenders in the league, strong, can move his feet, has got good size too. I feel like you're going to see a lot of different bodies on him and just try to wear him down over the course of a game and the course of the series.

quotes.speaker: Derrick White
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White reflects on the Celtics' 2024 playoff run
quotes.excerpt: We were not good enough there. It's hard to say it's a success when you lose in the playoffs.
quotes.quote: We definitely did a lot of things. Going into the year, nobody really knew what type of year we were going to have. It was fun just to go out there and change our identity, change the way we play, and for a lot of new guys to step up and get their first real opportunity. Jaylen Brown showed what he could do, and even seeing Jayson Tatum come back from his injury. We play for the Celtics and we get judged on what we do in the playoffs in the postseason, and we were not good enough there. It's hard to say it's a success when you lose in the playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Derrick White
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White on the importance of two-way play in the modern NBA
quotes.excerpt: That's how I got my foot in the door and how Pop started believing in me.
quotes.quote: That's how I got my foot in the door and how Pop started believing in me and trusting me was on the defensive end. We talk about defense all the time, and if you want to play, you got to be able to guard on both sides. I think we got a lot of guys that are two-way players and compete on both sides of the ball.

quotes.speaker: Derrick White
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White on the underrated defensive impact of NBA stars
quotes.excerpt: A lot of the stars they don't get enough credit for some of their defense.
quotes.quote: I think a lot of the stars they don't get enough credit for some of their defense because they got so much pressure offensively that they're not on the star players, so they don't get as much credit. I think Jaylen Brown does a really good job of taking that challenge, and it's fun to see him pick up full when you know he's going to get 30. I think Jayson Tatum also doesn't get enough credit as being a two-way.

quotes.speaker: Derrick White
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White on Joe Mazzulla's unique coaching style
quotes.excerpt: He's a great basketball mind. He thinks the game like no one I've really been around.
quotes.quote: He's a great basketball mind. He thinks the game like no one I've really been around. All the stories of him just being crazy just how he is every single day. It's not for the media, nothing. He just goes out there and he's like, all these stories that the media hears about me is like people telling it. I don't go out there and do all this stuff.

quotes.speaker: Derrick White
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White on Jaylen Brown's work ethic and focus
quotes.excerpt: I don't think people understand how hard he works. Every day he's in there working on his game.
quotes.quote: I don't think people understand how hard he works. Every day he's in there working on his game, working on different things he can improve, just watching film and just seeing different ways to improve. When you see that from behind the scenes, you want to play for him and you want to help in any way you can.

quotes.speaker: Derrick White
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White on the differences between winning an NBA title and Olympic gold
quotes.excerpt: The Olympic is so crazy because you got a month, two months to figure it out.
quotes.quote: The Olympic is so crazy because you got a month, two months to figure it out and we kind of all just come together and we all have to sacrifice. But it happens so quick. I think that's the biggest difference. NBA championship, we start in September and then you don't win until June, so it's like a long grind. And Olympics, especially when you get to the knockout stages, like one game and it's over with.
